about: The priest drops a small particle of the consecrated Host into the chalice. He quietly asks that this commingling and consecration of the Body and Blood of our Lord Jesus Christ may avail us unto eternal life.

s01.narrative: The priest lets the particle fall into the chalice, saying this secretly.

s02.translation: May this mingling and consecration of the Body and Blood of our Lord Jesus Christ bring eternal life to us who receive it. Amen.

w001.function: Feminine, agreeing with “commíxtio” (w002): this mingling — the one his fingers are making as he speaks.

w002.function: Con- and misceo: to mix one thing into another. In the whole Ordinary of the Mass the word occurs only here.

w004.function: The second subject of “fiat” (w012), and the verb stays singular: the two acts are counted as one thing done.

w011.function: The comma after it closes a chain of five nouns in the genitive — nostri agrees along with them — so that the reader does not lose the subject before the verb arrives.

w012.function: Subjunctive of wish — the prayer does not assert the effect, it asks for it.

w013.function: A participle agreeing with “nobis” (w014): to us as receiving, that is, in the act of receiving. The gift is asked for in the receiving, not merely for the recipients.

w014.function: Dative with “fiat” (w012): may it turn out so for us.

w018.function: Spoken by the priest himself and under his breath, like the rest of the sentence. There is no one to answer it.
